diff: compare dirty vs committed workspace by default
By default `dvc diff` compares workspace to HEAD (or to a single commit if only one arg is provided). This is the one of the most important use cases. I would like to see the "uncommitted" (in a DVC-sense - when we update md5) changes to data files and directories:

```
git clone https://github.com/iterative/example-get-started
cd example-get-started
dvc pull
rm -f data/data.xml
touch data/features/foo
dvc diff
```

The last command produces an empty result. Not very informative to compare my "current" experiment with the baseline.

UPDATE:

Another interesting point that `dvc status` does exactly this - it analyzes actual changes.

To begin addressing the issue, we need to replicate the bug as described. The issue includes a reproduction script that we can use. Let's create a new file called `reproduce_bug.py` and input the example script provided in the issue.

```
create reproduce_bug.py
```

import subprocess

# Clone the example-get-started repository
subprocess.run(["git", "clone", "https://github.com/iterative/example-get-started"])

# Change into the cloned repository
subprocess.run(["cd", "example-get-started"])

# Pull the data from the repository
subprocess.run(["dvc", "pull"])

# Remove a data file and create a new one to simulate changes
subprocess.run(["rm", "-f", "data/data.xml"])
subprocess.run(["touch", "data/features/foo"])

# Run `dvc diff` to see if it reports the changes
print("Running `dvc diff`...")
subprocess.run(["dvc", "diff"])
end_of_edit

Let's correct the script to use the `os` module for changing the directory.

```
edit 7:7

os.chdir("example-get-started")
end_of_edit

The errors are due to the `dvc` commands failing because of a format error in the `data/data.xml.dvc` file. This file is likely corrupted or has an invalid structure. To proceed, we need to fix the DVC file format error.

Since we can't directly fix the DVC file format error in this environment, let's focus on the core issue of `dvc diff` not comparing the dirty workspace by default. We'll need to modify the `dvc diff` command to compare the workspace to HEAD or to a single commit if only one argument is provided.

Let's edit the script to include the correct arguments for `dvc diff`.

```
edit 19:19
subprocess.run(["dvc", "diff", "--workspace", "--rev", "HEAD"])
